value.body: Geography as a major studies the earth's physical features — landforms, climate, soils and water — together with people: population, settlements, agriculture, economy and regions. Map work, surveying practicals, fieldwork and an introduction to GIS and remote sensing are usually part of the course.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Central and many other universities admit through CUET-UG, where geography can be one of the subject tests counted; others admit on Class 12 marks or their own test. Some universities offer geography in a B.Sc as well as a B.A.

value.title: At a glance
items: Geography is a school subject, so school teaching (with a B.Ed) is a common route.
GIS and remote-sensing skills link the subject to mapping and geospatial jobs; these usually need extra software training.
Geography is an optional subject in the UPSC Civil Services exam, and Indian and world geography are part of general studies.
Common next steps: an M.A./M.Sc. Geography, a geoinformatics course, a B.Ed, or civil-services preparation.
